questions.q: In the worked playbook, what happens during the 'ingest' step?
options: The forwarded phishing email lands in the mailbox and the SOAR platform picks it up as a new case
The email is immediately deleted without review
An analyst manually types the case details into the SOAR platform
The domain is blocked before any other step runs
questions.explain: Ingest is the entry point -- the SOAR platform picks up the new case via its API connection to the mailbox.

questions.q: What does the 'enrich' step do in this playbook?
options: Checks the extracted sender address and URL against threat intel feeds for outside context
Deletes the original email permanently
Sends the email to every employee for awareness training
Skips straight to notifying the analyst with no further checks
questions.explain: Enrichment adds outside context -- like a threat intel verdict -- before the playbook decides what to do next.

questions.q: What does the playbook do if the URL/domain is confirmed malicious by threat intel?
options: Auto-quarantines the email from every inbox it reached and blocks the domain at the email gateway
Takes no action and waits a week to see if more reports come in
Forwards the email to the original sender for clarification
Immediately isolates every endpoint in the company
questions.explain: A confirmed-malicious verdict triggers automatic containment: quarantine plus a gateway block for future copies.

questions.q: Why does the playbook notify an analyst even on the fully automated, confirmed-malicious branch?
options: So the analyst has a visible record, in case this report is part of a larger campaign worth investigating
Because the playbook is not actually allowed to take any automated action
Notification on that branch serves no real purpose and is just a formality
Because threat intel feeds require manual analyst approval before any lookup
questions.explain: Even with no decision left to make, a human needs visibility to spot patterns across multiple related reports.

questions.q: How does this worked example tie back to Lesson 25's three SOAR components?
options: Orchestration connects the mailbox, threat intel, and gateway; automation runs extraction/enrichment; response quarantines and blocks
The example only demonstrates automation and has nothing to do with orchestration or response
It shows that SOAR components only apply to EDR platforms, not email security
It proves that orchestration and automation are the same capability
questions.explain: The single scenario demonstrates all three SOAR capabilities working together on one real case.
